blocks.orig: Tanzania may be the country in Africa that people know the most about. It is the nation whose name has come to be associated with Zanzibar, Mount Kilimanjaro, and the Serengeti. Travelers from all over the world swarm to Tanzania to go on safari in some of the world’s top national parks.
blocks.html: Of all African countries, Tanzania is perhaps the one people know best. Its name has become linked with Zanzibar, Mount Kilimanjaro and the Serengeti. Visitors from every corner of the globe flock here to go on safari in some of the finest national parks on the planet.

blocks.orig: The nation is breathtakingly gorgeous, has a welcoming Swahili culture, and has some of the world’s best wildlife. Tanzania, though, is considerably more unique than you may think! Here are ten fascinating facts about Tanzania that might surprise you.
blocks.html: The country is stunningly beautiful, its Swahili culture is warm and welcoming, and its wildlife ranks among the best anywhere. Yet Tanzania is far more distinctive than you might expect! Below you’ll find ten intriguing facts about Tanzania that may well surprise you.

blocks.orig: 1. It Is Home To The Tallest Mountain In Africa
blocks.html: 1. Africa’s tallest mountain stands here

blocks.orig: If you’re fortunate enough to see it, this cone-shaped mountain covered in snow will amaze you! The highest freestanding peak in the world and the tallest mountain in Africa, Mount Kilimanjaro, is 5,895 meters above sea level. Almost every type of ecological system, including those found in cultivated land, the rainforest, the alpine desert, and the arctic peak, can be found there. You are more than welcome to take in the magnificence of this mountain from the ground, though those who are interested can climb this dormant volcano and see amazing views.
blocks.html: Should you be lucky enough to catch sight of it, this snow-capped, cone-shaped mountain will leave you in awe! At 5,895 meters above sea level, Mount Kilimanjaro is both Africa’s tallest mountain and the highest freestanding peak on earth. Nearly every kind of ecosystem occurs on its slopes, from cultivated land and rainforest to alpine desert and the arctic summit. You are very welcome to admire this majestic mountain from below, while anyone keen can climb the dormant volcano and enjoy spectacular views.

blocks.orig: 2. Over 1.5 Million Animals Travel During The Great Migration
blocks.html: 2. More than 1.5 million animals take part in the Great Migration

blocks.orig: Over 1.5 million wildebeest, zebra, and gazelles travel through the plains of Tanzania and Kenya during the Great Wildebeest Migration in search of pasture. The crossing of the Mara River, where vast herds of animals make their way to the Masai Mara while dodging crocodiles and other dangers, is unquestionably the most thrilling aspect of this incredible event.
blocks.html: In the Great Wildebeest Migration, upwards of 1.5 million wildebeest, zebra and gazelles move across the plains of Tanzania and Kenya looking for grazing. Without doubt the most dramatic moment of this remarkable spectacle is the Mara River crossing, where enormous herds head for the Masai Mara while evading crocodiles and other threats.

blocks.orig: 3. Nearly 30% Of Tanzania Is National Parks
blocks.html: 3. National parks cover almost 30% of Tanzania

blocks.orig: Tanzania is home to some of the world’s top national parks. One of the most well-known and adored parks is the Serengeti National Park, which is home to more than a million different species of large mammals. In addition to being a World Heritage Site, it has the distinction of being the 7th World Wonder. Wildebeest and zebras travel across the plains of the Serengeti during the Great Migration in search of new grasslands. Great buffalo herds, elephants, giraffes, leopards, impala, gazelles, and the endangered Eastern black rhinoceros can all be found there too. The Selous Game Reserve is home to the biggest population of elephants, which are also found in Tanzania. Gombe Stream National Park, another well-known park in Tanzania, is where Dr. Jane Goodall famously conducted her chimpanzee research.
blocks.html: Some of the finest national parks on earth lie in Tanzania. Among the best known and most loved is Serengeti National Park, where more than a million different species of large mammals live. Besides being a World Heritage Site, it also holds the title of 7th World Wonder. During the Great Migration, wildebeest and zebras cross the Serengeti plains looking for fresh grasslands. You will also find large buffalo herds, elephants, giraffes, leopards, impala, gazelles and the endangered Eastern black rhinoceros. Tanzania is home to elephants too, with the largest population living in the Selous Game Reserve. Gombe Stream National Park, another famous Tanzanian park, is where Dr. Jane Goodall carried out her well-known research on chimpanzees.

blocks.orig: 4. Lake Tanganyika Is The Second-Largest Lake In The World
blocks.html: 4. Lake Tanganyika ranks as the world’s second-largest lake

blocks.orig: Second only to Lake Baikal in Siberia in terms of volume and depth, Lake Tanganyika is one of the largest freshwater lakes in the world. Due to its size, it is divided among four nations: Tanzania, Burundi, Zambia, and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. The lake is one of the most biologically diverse and important environments in the world. It is supplied by at least 50 streams and rivers. 500 different kinds of fish live in Lake Tanganyika, which contains an incredible 8% of the world’s freshwater. Most of these fish remain within 20 meters of the surface.
blocks.html: Lake Tanganyika is among the biggest freshwater lakes on the planet, surpassed in volume and depth only by Lake Baikal in Siberia. It is so large that four countries share it: Tanzania, Burundi, Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo. As an environment, the lake is one of the richest in biodiversity and most significant anywhere. At least 50 rivers and streams feed it. Holding a remarkable 8% of the world’s freshwater, Lake Tanganyika supports 500 different fish species, the majority of which stay within 20 meters of the surface.

blocks.orig: 5. Tanzania Has A Unique Species Of Tree-Climbing Lions
blocks.html: 5. Tanzania has a special kind of tree-climbing lion

blocks.orig: Tree-climbing lions can be found in Tarangire National Park. It is unknown why these lions have started climbing. It’s debatable whether they do it to catch a cool breeze or to get clear of the tsetse flies. Of course, it’s also possible that the lions are just admiring the scenery from above. Whatever their motivations, it is impressive to watch these lions cautiously traverse the tree branches.
blocks.html: In Tarangire National Park you can come across lions that climb trees. Nobody knows for sure why they began doing this. Some say it helps them catch a cooling breeze, others that it keeps them away from tsetse flies. Then again, the lions may simply be enjoying the view from up high. Whatever the reason, watching them carefully pick their way along the branches is a striking sight.

blocks.orig: 6. Ngorongoro Crater Is One Of The Best Places To See The Big Five
blocks.html: 6. Ngorongoro Crater is among the top spots to see the Big Five

blocks.orig: The internationally known Ngorongoro Crater, which is situated in northern Tanzania, is another must-visit location. This rich valley, which is thought to have been created by a volcanic explosion, is one of the most stunning places in the world for a wildlife safari and has even been named one of Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders. The crater’s constricted nature has given rise to a unique ecology that provides some of the best chances to see game. Additionally, it boasts the highest known density of lions. In addition to a variety of other well-known African icons like the ostrich, zebra, cheetah, wildebeest, gazelle, and even hippos, you can witness buffalo, elephants, leopards, and rhinoceroses here.
blocks.html: Located in northern Tanzania, the world-famous Ngorongoro Crater is another place you should not miss. Believed to have been formed by a volcanic eruption, this fertile valley is one of the most beautiful settings anywhere for a wildlife safari and has even been listed among Africa’s Seven Natural Wonders. Because the crater is so enclosed, a distinctive ecosystem has developed here that offers some of the best game-viewing opportunities. It also has the highest density of lions known. Here you can see buffalo, elephants, leopards and rhinoceroses, as well as many other famous African animals such as the ostrich, zebra, cheetah, wildebeest, gazelle and even hippos.

blocks.orig: 7. Olduvai Gorge Has Human Fossils From Millions Of Years Ago
blocks.html: 7. Olduvai Gorge holds human fossils millions of years old

blocks.orig: One of the most intriguing facts about Tanzania is that ancient human bones were discovered in Olduvai Gorge, home to one of the country’s most picturesque lakes. These ancient humanoid bones, which date back millions of years, are proof of the existence of the first humans. Among what was found was the oldest human skull ever unearthed.
blocks.html: A particularly fascinating fact about Tanzania is that ancient human remains were found in Olduvai Gorge, where one of the most scenic lakes in the country lies. Millions of years old, these early humanoid bones show that the first humans existed. The discoveries included the oldest human skull ever found.

blocks.orig: 8. Zanzibar Was The Center Of Arab Slave Trade
blocks.html: 8. Zanzibar was the hub of the Arab slave trade

blocks.orig: Slaves were long traded in Zanzibar by Arab and Indian traders, in addition to Portuguese and other Europeans. People were one of the main commodities here. It’s sad to say that a significant portion of the Zanzibar trade involved slavery. The final active slave market in the world was located in the heart of Stone Town. In Zanzibar, it is currently a significant historical site. A total of 40–50,000 slaves were sent to Zanzibar every year, many of whom worked on the plantations of the area that was then ruled by the Omani. Under British pressure, it shut down in 1873.
blocks.html: For a long time, Arab and Indian traders, as well as the Portuguese and other Europeans, traded slaves in Zanzibar. Human beings were among the key goods sold here, and it is sad to say that slavery made up a large share of the trade on Zanzibar. The last active slave market in the world stood in the centre of Stone Town and today it is an important historical site on Zanzibar. Each year some 40–50,000 slaves were shipped to Zanzibar, and many were put to work on plantations in the region, which was ruled by the Omani at that time. The market closed in 1873 under pressure from the British.

blocks.orig: 9. It Has Some Of The Most Beautiful Waterfalls In Africa
blocks.html: 9. Some of Africa’s loveliest waterfalls are found here

blocks.orig: Tanzania has a lot of lakes and mountains, so it makes sense that there would be waterfalls as well. One of the most breathtaking waterfalls in Africa is without a doubt Kalambo Falls near the border of Zambia and the Rukwa Region. The water descends 772 feet in a single, unbroken drop, making it one of the highest uninterrupted falls on the continent. It is an extension of the Kalambo River located on the border between Zambia and the Songwe Region. Given that it has been inhabited for more than 200,000 years, it is also a significant archaeological site. Another fantastic activity for a day spent away from the hustle and bustle of daily life is a trip of the Materuni Waterfalls. Tanzania’s natural beauty may be seen on the hike to Materuni Waterfall, near the Kilimanjaro Region.
blocks.html: With so many lakes and mountains in Tanzania, it is no surprise that the country has waterfalls too. Kalambo Falls, close to the border of Zambia and the Rukwa Region, is undoubtedly one of the most spectacular in Africa. Its water plunges 772 feet in one continuous drop, which makes it one of the tallest uninterrupted falls in Africa. It forms part of the Kalambo River on the border between Zambia and the Songwe Region. People have lived here for more than 200,000 years, so it is an important archaeological site as well. A visit to the Materuni Waterfalls is another great way to spend a day far from the rush of everyday life. On the hike to Materuni Waterfall, close to the Kilimanjaro Region, you get to see Tanzania’s natural beauty.

blocks.orig: 10. The Shortest War In History Took Place Here
blocks.html: 10. History’s shortest war was fought here

blocks.orig: The Anglo-Zanzibar War, which took place in Tanzania in 1896 and lasted less than an hour. It was between 38 and 45 minutes, to be exact. It all began because the British did not want the previous Sultan’s successor to be in command. They desired Hamud bin Muhammad, who was friendlier to the British. The British gave an ultimatum and asked that the successor be changed. The British Navy opened fire on the palace with 4,100 machine gun rounds, 1,000 rifle rounds, and 500 shells since the new Sultan wasn’t willing to cooperate. The frenzy came to an end, and the British accomplished their goal. ‍
blocks.html: The Anglo-Zanzibar War was fought in Tanzania in 1896 and was over in under an hour – between 38 and 45 minutes, to be precise. The conflict started because the British did not want the late Sultan’s successor in power. Their preferred candidate was Hamud bin Muhammad, who was more favourable towards the British. They issued an ultimatum demanding a different successor. Because the new Sultan refused to cooperate, the British Navy fired 4,100 machine gun rounds, 1,000 rifle rounds and 500 shells at the palace. The chaos ended and the British got what they wanted. ‍

blocks.orig: Baobab trees can live to be 1,000 years old. They can be seen in Tarangire National Park, along with the tree-climbing lions. The oldest one, found in South Africa, is believed to be 6,000 years old.
blocks.html: Baobab trees can reach an age of 1,000 years. In Tarangire National Park you can see them alongside the tree-climbing lions. The oldest known baobab, in South Africa, is thought to be 6,000 years old.

blocks.orig: Germany used to rule Tanzania until the end of World War 1, when the British took over. It ceased to be a part of the British Empire in 1961.
blocks.html: Tanzania was ruled by Germany until the close of World War 1, after which the British took control. In 1961 it stopped being part of the British Empire.

blocks.orig: Tanzania has more languages than any other African country. It has over 100 languages, however, the national languages of Tanzania are English and Swahili.
blocks.html: No other African country has as many languages as Tanzania. More than 100 are spoken, although English and Swahili are the national languages.

blocks.orig: It is home to Africa’s highest point and lowest point. The highest is the peak of Mount Kilimanjaro, while the lowest is the floor of Lake Tanganyika.
blocks.html: Both the highest and the lowest point in Africa lie in Tanzania. The summit of Mount Kilimanjaro is the highest, and the bed of Lake Tanganyika the lowest.

blocks.orig: Freddie Mercury was born in Tanzania. The Queen frontman was born to Parsi-Indian parents in Zanzibar, and fled to Middlesex, UK, in 1964 during the Zanzibar Revolution.
blocks.html: Tanzania is the birthplace of Freddie Mercury. The Queen frontman was born on Zanzibar to Parsi-Indian parents and left for Middlesex, UK, in 1964 during the Zanzibar Revolution.

blocks.orig: Tanzania is home to over 100 tribes, who each have their own tribal language and religion. These tribes live in harmony with one another, and are able to live together peacefully and respect each other’s decisions when it comes to culture and religion, including those who follow Christianity and Islam.
blocks.html: More than 100 tribes live in Tanzania, each with its own tribal language and religion. They coexist in harmony, living side by side peacefully and respecting one another’s choices on culture and religion, including followers of Christianity and Islam.

blocks.orig: There is much more to Tanzania than meets the eye. It is an incredibly fascinating country with a rich history and interesting culture, as well as stunning landscapes. These were just some truly amazing facts about the African country.
blocks.html: Tanzania has far more to offer than you might see at first glance. It is a truly fascinating country with a rich past, an interesting culture and beautiful scenery. These were only a few of the remarkable facts about this African country.
